title: Switching The Policy Rate
text:
Switching The Policy Rate

Wei He

Gavekal Dragonomics | 27 Oct 2026

The People’s Bank of China has not cut policy interest rates in more than a year, but some market participants claim that a stealth cut is now underway. On October 19, PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng announced that the central bank would change its main policy rate from the seven-day reverse repo to the overnight reverse repo. The PBOC has reportedly set its overnight rate 15 bp lower than the seven-day tenor, leading to the claims of a de facto cut.The switch will indeed have some effects similar to a rate cut, such as cheaper funding for commercial banks and lower bond yields. But it will not lead to lower rates for most borrowers, and a stealth monetary easing is not the PBOC’s intent: it is switching the policy rate primarily to bring its monetary-policy framework into line with other major central banks. It will continue to keep rates—and in turn bond yields—relatively low and steady in order to facilitate government bond issuance, but is likely to materially lower the policy rate only if economic growth slows further.
